title: Distributed purge consistency checker and customer-facing certification
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers requesting Right-To-Be-Forgotten (RTBF) or retention-driven purges need cryptographic, machine-verifiable proof that records have been erased across all storage strata (primary DBs, cold backups, snapshot archives, caches, and private Dedicated nodes). Current deletion workflows record completion events but do not provide a deterministic way to assert cross-shard consistency or to surface divergence windows to customers or auditors.

Goal: Build a distributed purge consistency checker that produces an anchored, signed evidence package customers can download and validate. The system must detect divergence (e.g., tombstone not propagated to backup snapshot, cache miss, or regional replica lag), auto-open remediation tickets for high-severity divergences, and expose a simple customer-facing certificate containing an expiration-bound verification token and provenance manifests.

Scope:
- Produce signed purge manifests per-tenant (JSONL) containing per-shard attestations and per-store hashes.
- Implement cross-store reconciliation that runs post-purge and again at T+24h and T+7d for a rolling window of consistency checks.
- Integrate with Console to allow customer download of a "Purge Certificate" and a machine-readable evidence bundle for third-party auditors.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not include full legal boilerplate for varying jurisdictions. That will be follow-up with Legal.
- Does not replace data-retention policy editor UI; assumes retention decisions come from existing policy engine.
acceptance_criteria: For a simulated tenant purge, system emits a signed evidence bundle (manifest.jsonl + per-store attestations) within 30 minutes of purge completion
Cross-store reconciliation runs produce a human-readable divergence report and machine-readable remediation actions if any inconsistency is detected
Console displays a downloadable Purge Certificate with verification token and hash summary; token validates against internal verification API
Automated remediation opens ENG tickets for high-severity divergences and triggers a one-time re-purge workflow for affected shards
Audit-runner harness verifies evidence bundles for 95% of synthetic purge cases in CI within the 3-hour test window
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: Kickoff with Eng (Owen Patel) and Security (Aisha Verma). Agreed on threat model: attacker cannot tamper with signed manifests stored in the compliance ledger without KMS compromise.

2026-02-22: Design doc posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPLIANCE/Distributed+Purge+Consistency+Checker. Chosen approach: per-shard hash + aggregate Merkle-like root anchored in internal ledger with HSM-backed signing.

2026-02-28: Eng spike completed (ENG-2081). Prototype reconciliation job that compares primary DB tombstones against S3 snapshot manifests. Found a 3% divergence in test dataset due to snapshot timing — added T+24h pass requirement.
2026-03-05: UX mocks for Console certificate download reviewed by Design (see attachments). PM feedback: certificate must clearly indicate when the evidence expires and how to validate offline.

2026-03-10: Security review flagged key rotation handling for long-lived evidence. Decision: evidence bundles will include key-version metadata and a short-lived verification token; Legal to review retention of evidence bundles separately.
review_feedback: Design (Eve Nakamura): prefer a compact certificate summary in addition to full evidence bundle for non-technical customers
Security (Aisha Verma): add explicit KMS key-version in manifest and require HSM signing for production release
Engineering (Owen Patel): suggested adding a 'reconciliation severity' field with values {ok, transient, stuck, missing} to drive runbook steps
Legal (Phil Sokolov, note): jurisdictional footprint must be surfaced on certificate when purge involves cross-region replicas
notes: Operator runbook draft: add step to escalate to on-call infra team if 'stuck' severity persists beyond 2 hours
Evidence format: newline-delimited JSON where each line is an object {store, shard_id, timestamp, hash, signer_key_version}
Verification API: /v1/compliance/verify?token=<token> returns signed status and list of store checks; rate-limited to protect privacy
Rollout plan: start with non-customer-facing internal pilot for 2 weeks, then opt-in beta for 5 customers, then GA
Open question: should we store customer-downloadable evidence bundles encrypted at rest with tenant-specific keys? Security prefers yes; impacts Dedicated/private designs.
